findings.title: Leader reaping precedes later raw numeric process-group signals
source_evidence: Owner stop_wait starts with proc.poll(), then proc.wait(timeout=10); main also polls at192/210 and waits at216/218. Finally224-230 tests and signals numeric adapter/native group IDs after these paths may have reaped the adapter.
Caller polls at233/244/247/258/263/271 and waits at261/264/272, then killpg(process.pid,0) and SIGKILL at275/277 use the reaped native leader number.

The caller timer stop function polls and then raw-signals at233-235 while main-thread polls/waits are outside that lock. cancel at269 supplies no source-level callback-quiescence proof before further wait/group operations.
findings.impact: A prior PID/PGID observation or killpg(g,0) liveness test does not retain an unreaped ownership anchor. After leader reaping and numeric ID reuse, a later raw killpg can address a group that is no longer the admitted group. This is a source race, not an observed mis-signal.
findings.correction_direction: Retain one strong unreaped certified leader through the final authorized group signals. Use nonreaping exit observation, then exact-PID bounded deliberate reap after no further group signals are intended. Remove every post-reap raw group signal and serialize timer/stop/ownership transitions.

findings.impact: A separate native session can be missed between discovery and adapter stop, and root has no retained anchor for discovered groups after the caller reaps them. Native should not detach into a second session under this design. Keeping separate groups would require a separately specified, failure-safe ownership handoff and wider review.
